content:
I have noticed that when applying mkLambdaFVars over an mvar, this mvar ends up being assigned. This is annoying for my usecase because the mvar was meant to be a new goal in my tactic. I'd be curious to know:
(1) Why does mkLambdaFVars have this behaviour?
(2) How does one get around it?

Small MWE

import Lean
open Lean Meta in

run_meta do
  let (expr, mvar) ← withLocalDeclD `x (.const `Nat []) fun x => do
    let mvar ← Meta.mkFreshExprMVar (Expr.const `Nat [])
    pure (← mkLambdaFVars #[x] mvar, mvar)

  logInfo s!"{expr}"
  let mvarId := mvar.mvarId!
  if ← mvarId.isAssigned then
    let mctx ← getMCtx
    logError s!"😕\n?{mvarId.name} is assigned to {mctx.eAssignment.find? mvarId |>.get!}"
  else
    logInfo s!"🎉\n?{mvarId.name} is not assigned!"
(deleted). That was not correct. Sorry, I should not postulate stuff, when I'm on a hurry.

I've been able to work around the issue by creating the lambda metavariable first, and then doing mvar.intro to receive a new mvar and the fvar it introduced. That way, the final mvar will have the shape I wanted, and it's guaranteed to not have been assigned. However, I wanted to understand further why the current behaviour is as it is, althought it might not be anything grand, just a "well, it's just how it makes sense to implement it"
if your metavariable is supposed to be a tactic goal, you should make it synthetic opaque

Don't use regular metavariables for tactic states. You should use docs#Lean.Meta.mkFreshExprSyntheticOpaqueMVar and not docs#Lean.Meta.mkFreshExprMVar for tactics. The reason that mkLambdaFVars assigns metavariables is the following:

  • We generate some metavariable ?m : α and try to mkLambdaFVars with x
  • If you'd not do anything with metavariables, you'll end up with fun x : Nat => ?m and we have a problem: ?m needs a variable x : Nat in its local context but the variable no longer exists in the local context and instead as a binder. Furthermore, it would seem like fun x : Nat => ?m is constant/does not depend on x! Oh no!
  • The solution: delayed assigned metavariables. We create a new metavariable ?n : Nat → α and "synchronize" it with ?m (or well, create a delayed assignment). Basically, we say "whenever ?m gets assigned, assign n to mkLambdaFVars #[x] (assignment of ?m)". Well not quite, since in reality this happens lazily, but this is the idea. Then we can just use fun x : Nat => ?n x!
  • Now, problem solved, right? Well, no, the problem is ?n is now assigned (even if just delayed). If isDefEq tried to do anything here, it couldn't. So what actually happens for non-synthetic-opaque metavariables is that we create a regular metavariable ?n and assign ?m to ?n x (the opposite).
Hmm, I see, and since delayed assignment is not assignment, I am able to assign to it even if it's already delayed assigned?
Well, you shouldn't. That's why I said that isDefEq can't do anything with delayed assignment.
If you would assign a delayed assigned metavariable, you'd override the value it would eventually have (i.e. its value of mkLambdaFVars #[x] (assignment of ?m))

As I said, you need to synchronize ?n x with ?m one way or another. One way is to assign ?m := ?n x and that's what it will prefer (and what you don't what if you want to treat ?m as a tactic metavariable) and the other is the delayed assignment ?n x := ?m which doesn't touch ?m (that's what you want for tactic metavariables).
I see, I had missunderstood that ?m was the metavariable delay assigned, but no, it's ?n. Thanks!
